h: The Enduring Name of Yisrael and Torah Within the Heart

p: "Hear the word of Hashem, House of Yaakov,
וְכָל מִשְׁפְּחוֹת בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל (יִרְמְיָה ב, ד)
and all the families of the House of Israel" (Yirmiyahu 2:4).
even at the time of corruption
by the names Yaakov and Yisrael,
and their name was not lost.
that it brought this parable specifically here?
before you will have to hear outside the Land";
that is, that in the end
it will be that they hear,
כֵּן יִהְיֶה דְבָרִי אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵא מִפִּי
"So shall My word be that goes out of My mouth;
it shall not return to Me empty,
כִּי אִם עָשָׂה אֶת אֲשֶׁר חָפַצְתִּי
but it shall do what I desire
And along the lines of what they said (Berachos 6b):
כָּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
"Every person who has fear of Heaven
'The end of the matter, all having been heard,'" etc.
a person who has fear of Heaven
becomes a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב הַקְדָּמַת זוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ ה, ב)
(as is written, Introduction to the holy Zohar, 5b);
and he is in the aspect of
"My word that goes out of My mouth";
and therefore his words are heeded.
And it is written, "The end of the matter, all is heard":
even if he is not heeded at the time,
And so the word of Hashem
and succeed in that for which I sent it";
and if they are not heeded in their time,
in the end they will be heeded.
And this is what it says:
"Hear the word of Hashem in Eretz Yisrael,"
for in the end they will hear outside the Land.
and "the families of the House of Israel,"
"our will is to do Your will,
The leaven in the dough," etc.
הַכֹּהֲנִים לֹא אָמְרוּ אַיֵּה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
"The Kohanim did not say, Where is Hashem," etc.;
for about the shepherds it says,
who were occupied with the avodah
the place where the Shechinah rests
וְהֵם הָיָה לָהֶם לֵידַע אַיֵּה ה׳
they should have known "Where is Hashem,"
seeing the resting of the Shechinah:
in the midst of the Children of Israel."
which was instituted in place of the daily offerings,
like one standing before the King.
And about this it says, "The Kohanim":
for they were not in the state of
the main purpose of Torah study
is that it act upon the heart;
"May He open our heart in His Torah"
and hear the words of the wise,
and set your heart to My knowledge;
for it is pleasant if you keep them within you."
And this is that the main thing is Da'as;
this is one who recognizes his Creator,"
and knowledge is pleasant to your soul"
that when wisdom enters the heart,
And it explains, "pleasant to your soul":
that he will feel taste in words of Torah;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב לא, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (II 31b).
And this is what it says, "For it is pleasant," etc.;
"And by knowledge the chambers are filled
with all precious and pleasant wealth."
"Then you will understand the fear of Hashem
and find the knowledge of God."
And this is what it says:
with all precious and pleasant wealth,"
which is the aspect of Binah;
that is, that he will feel taste and pleasantness
and this is the meaning of "for it is pleasant."
"if you keep them within you (in your belly)"
"if you keep them in your heart";
in the name of a Midrash:
that words of Torah enter his body,
that delicacies not enter his body."
that it not enter his innards."
And this is because the yetzer hara rules
"And you shall eat and be satisfied;
lest your heart be enticed," etc.;
And this is "if you keep them within you":
that the eating be in holiness;
and then "they will be established together on your lips."
And this is what the prophet says:
"And those who grasp the Torah did not know Me"
that they did not merit Da'as.
is that the intent be for the sake of Heaven,
and then they merit what is said,
I have not drunk a revi'is of wine,
being the son-in-law of the Nasi's household,
meat and wine for words of Torah,
so that his mind would be clear;
and the eating and drinking were
in holiness, for the sake of Heaven,
and then he merits the aspect of Da'as.
And so each one of Yisrael merits
when the eating is in holiness,
and they merit words of Torah
and "knowledge is pleasant to your soul";
and they merit to hear the word of Hashem.
And this is why every year we read as haftarah
perhaps we will merit to hear now
the word of Hashem, so that it enters the heart.

Service and Torah Must Seek the King
Holy Eating Opens the Heart to Torah
